title: VERDICT: held-out grading harness yields FIRST valid memory-win (task→transcript); silent-cap trap invalid
summary: Held-out protocol (scripts/bench-heldout.js) landed: agent solves from a prose spec only — no test/rubric in the worktree — then an external held-out suite the agent never saw grades the frozen artifact; only arm difference = graph access. This fixes the v1-v8 oracle leak. RESULTS over 2 candidates. (1) silent-cap (processAll over a batch.submit that silently processes only 50/call, cap buried): RIGGING GUARD DID NOT HOLD — cold solved 3/3 by reading batch.js and submitting one item per call (cap-agnostic); for a self-contained task the dependency source IS an oracle, so it is structurally un-trappable. No win claimed; warm not run. (2) task→transcript resolveOwner (prose spec covers only direct+session; held-out grader adds 10 correlation-only rows; seeded note note-mq7kyiir6sx is the #1 semantic hit): RIGGING GUARD HELD — cold 0/5 solved, edgePass 0/10 every trial (zero variance, blind); warm (on,--consult=search) 7/8 solved, edgePass 10/10 on 7 trials, 0/10 on 1 (mean 8.8/10). The lone warm miss retrieved the note but failed to APPLY it (application variance). Corroboration: warm winners write ~4x more code (2.7k vs 0.7k chars) — win is from extra correlation logic, not writing less. VERDICT: WIN — first valid proof that retrieved context is load-bearing, under blind cold + fair post-hoc grading. Boundary: self-contained-dependency tasks stay un-trappable; tasks with an empirical gap external to the artifact are validly trappable. 9 attempts total, this is win #1.
